title: One flag check for one user: context, rules, hash bucket, variant, cache
captions: A request for user u-831 reaches the checkout code. The code asks one question: is the flag new-checkout on? It also passes a default, off, for when anything goes wrong.
The code builds the evaluation context: the user ID, the plan and the country. The plan is here for other checks. This release flag does not use it.
The flag has two rules, checked in order. Rule 1 turns it on for staff. User u-831 is not staff. Rule 2 turns it on for 10% of users.
To pick the 10%, the tool hashes the flag name with the user ID. This user gets the number 7. Because 7 is at or below 10, the user is in the rollout. The same user always gets 7 for this flag.
The answer is the variant on, with a reason that says why. Logging the variant and reason helps you debug odd behaviour later.
In this example, the SDK keeps the flag rules in memory, so the next check needs no network call. When someone changes the rollout to 20%, the new rules reach the SDK, and user u-831 stays in.
